notable_absence.finding: The timeout setting's own description says only 'You should not need to adjust the default setting to tune performance' without ever stating what the default numeric value actually IS - the page asserts a sensible default exists but never discloses it, unlike os-level-tuning.md in this same batch, which does give max_file_descriptors' default (5000) explicitly.

cross_component_finding: This page is explicit that a webhook filter can only decide WHETHER to post a document, never WHICH PARTS of it: 'Filtering only determines which documents to post. It does not extract specific content from documents and post only that.' Combined with the CAUTION admonition ('Webhooks post your application's data, which might include user data, to URLs. Consider the security implications.'), this means there is no field-level redaction capability anywhere in the webhook mechanism - a document is posted whole or not at all. See also changes-feed.json's cross_component_finding for this page's near-identical opening paragraph and shared comparison table with changes-feed.md.
cross_product_finding: The unsupported.remote_config_tls_skip_verify escape hatch mentioned here ('Setting this true will side-step essential security checks. Do not use in Production deployments') for externally-hosted HTTPS JavaScript functions is the same disable-verification-but-keep-encryption shape already recorded on the security/ batch's TLS settings (sgw:bootstrap-server-tls-skip-verify) - a recurring pattern across this product of pairing every TLS trust-chain verification step with its own named, explicitly-labeled-unsupported bypass flag.
